errors.forbiddenHint: You do not have permission to perform this action.

errors.conflictHint: A resource with the same identifier already exists.

auth.loginSubtitle: Manage your firewall, agents and traffic from a single control plane.
auth.passkeyFailed: the passkey could not be verified
auth.setupSubtitle: This is the first account — it will have administrator privileges.
auth.setupNotice: No users exist yet. Create the admin account to get started.
auth.invalidEmail: Please enter a valid email address
auth.passwordTooShort: Password must be at least {{min}} characters

account.title: Account administration
account.description: Dashboard users and the API keys that reach this control plane. Personal settings (profile, password, passkeys) live under your account card in Settings.

users.title: Dashboard users
users.description: Accounts that can sign in to this console, with their role, status and most recent login. Role and status changes revoke the account's outstanding tokens immediately.
users.createdHint: The account is created with the password you set; its holder can change it after signing in.
users.emailHint: Changing the login name revokes the account's outstanding tokens.
users.disableDescription: The account can no longer sign in and its outstanding tokens are revoked. Re-enable it at any time.
users.resetPasswordHint: The account must replace this password at its next sign-in, and every outstanding session is revoked immediately. The user is not notified - tell them out of band.
users.selfRoleHint: Your own role cannot be changed here; the last enabled administrator always survives.
users.error: Could not load the user list

forceChange.title: Replace your password
forceChange.description: This account was created with a temporary password. Choose a new one to continue - the console keeps refusing writes until the password is changed.

policies.overview: A policy is a named, revisioned configuration every assigned site follows: engine posture, custom rules, rule tuning, rate limits, IP access and imported CRS rulesets. Sites keep their own settings until you assign a policy on their Policy tab; site-local deltas belong in the site overlay. Every change is recorded in the policy history.
policies.title: WAF policies
policies.description: Shared, revisioned rule and posture documents. Assign a policy to a site to apply it; sites without a policy keep their own settings.
policies.newHint: A policy starts empty. Add its engine, CRS and custom-rule layers in the editor, then assign it to sites.
policies.templateHint: Pick a built-in starter posture, or start blank.
policies.recipeHint: Recipes are reviewed, parameterized rules; applying one adds it to the policy's custom rules.
policies.name: Policy name
policies.deleteBody: Deleting "{{name}}" removes it from {{n}} site(s). Those sites fall back to their own settings.
policies.emptyBody: Create a policy to share rule and posture tuning across sites.
policies.planHint: What the data plane will do with each managed rule, with the draft applied.
policies.historyHint: Every policy change is recorded; select a version to see what changed, or restore one as a new revision.
policies.testHint: Evaluate one sample request with the same native engine the edge runs. Rate limits, IP/geo access and bot checks are edge decisions and are reported as skipped.
policies.diffNone: No content changes between these versions.
policies.saveHint: Saved here, applied to every site following this policy on the next sync.
policies.editorBanner: This is a shared policy: changes are published here and reach the edge on the next sync (published ≠ applied - see Apply status on a site's Policy tab). Use Test to try the resolved configuration against a sample request first.

fields.modeHint: How matched attacks are answered. Unset keeps the site's own setting (or derives it from its rules).
fields.engineModeHint: inherit follows the process-wide engine switch.
fields.monitorCategoriesLinkage: A policy's family rules are monitored through the CRS layer's managed-rule list; only the site's Web Protection switches move both lists together.
fields.monitorHint: Matched attacks in these families are recorded, never blocked.
fields.monitorManagedRulesHint: Built-in managed rules downgraded to detect-and-log for every site following this policy.
fields.noRules: No custom rules in this policy yet.
fields.ruleExpressionHint: Rule language expression, e.g. http.request.uri.path eq "/probe".
fields.ruleTuningHint: Per-rule tuning applied to every site following this policy: monitor records findings without enforcing, disable skips the rule entirely, score override replaces its anomaly contribution.
fields.excludeTargetsHint: A match that depends on an excluded target is suppressed.
fields.virtualPatchHint: Virtual patches evaluated by the native engine before the managed rules.
fields.apiSchemaHint: Requests are validated against this document (shape checks are monitor-only).
fields.apiSchemaShape: The document must be a JSON object
fields.botWhitelistHint: User-agent tokens that are never treated as bots.
fields.crsImportRulesetHint: Imported rules compile into the same SecLang source the edge already evaluates as virtual patches.
fields.crsImportEmpty: No rulesets imported yet — import one on the CRS rules page first.
fields.crsImportCounts: {{supported}} rules compile, {{unsupported}} do not, {{directives}} directives recorded.
fields.crsImportParanoiaHint: Rules above this level are not sent to the edge. Unset keeps every compiled rule.
fields.rlEmpty: No shared rate limits in this policy yet.
fields.ipEmpty: No shared IP access rules in this policy yet.
fields.ipRangesHint: Addresses or CIDRs; the rule action applies to all of them.

crs.overview: Import an OWASP CRS archive (GitHub release, URL or upload) once and this engine parses it with its own SecLang parser. Rules it can compile are enforceable through a policy's CRS ruleset layer; rules it cannot compile stay visible with their parser error - nothing is dropped silently. Bind rulesets on the Policy tab.
crs.title: CRS rulesets
crs.description: Import OWASP CRS archives, inspect the parsed rule catalogue and bind rulesets to policies.
crs.importHint: Fetch a release from GitHub or point at an archive URL. Rules are parsed with this engine's SecLang parser; unsupported rules stay visible with their error.
crs.releasesUnavailable: GitHub is unreachable — type a tag or use a URL.
crs.name: Display name
crs.emptyBody: Import a CRS archive to browse its rules and bind them to policies.
crs.deleteBody: "{{name}}" will be removed. Bound policies: {{n}} — unbind them first if the delete is refused.
crs.catalogHint: Each row keeps its file/line provenance; rules this engine cannot compile are listed with their parser error.

alerts.overview: Rules evaluate stored security events on a timer: a raw count, or a blocked-request ratio gated by a minimum sample count so a single probe cannot page anyone. Preview shows what the next evaluation would see and dispatches nothing. Silences mute rules for maintenance; the history records every dispatched alert even when delivery fails.
alerts.title: Alerts & notifications
alerts.description: Alert rules over security events, maintenance silences, delivery channels, thresholds and the alert history - one page for everything an alert touches.
alerts.rulesHint: Counts fire at a raw number; ratios require a minimum sample count so a single blocked probe cannot page anyone.
alerts.noRulesHint: Create a rule to be told when blocked traffic spikes or a specific rule starts firing.
alerts.name: Name
alerts.thresholdInvalid: Must be a positive number (≤ 100 for ratios)
alerts.minSamplesHint: Requests required in the window before the ratio counts.
alerts.cooldownHint: Minimum time between two firings of this rule.
alerts.eventTypeHint: Currently the agents stamp every WAF decision as 'waf'.
alerts.ruleIdContainsHint: Substring filter over the rule id.
alerts.channelsHint: Delivery targets for every alert. Secrets are sealed at rest; leave the redacted placeholder to keep the stored value.
alerts.previewHint: What the next evaluation would see. Nothing is dispatched by a preview.
alerts.previewNote: Window {{window}}s; ratios require {{samples}} samples before they count.
alerts.ruleDialogHint: A rule evaluates stored security events; it never inspects live traffic itself.
alerts.silencesHint: Active and scheduled maintenance windows. Silences are recorded with their author.
alerts.noSilences: No silences - every rule is live.
alerts.silenceDialogHint: Mute alert rules for a maintenance window. A global silence mutes every rule; a site silence mutes rules scoped to that site.
alerts.noChannels: No channels yet - alerts are recorded in the history but nothing is delivered.
alerts.urlHint: Must be a public http(s) URL; internal addresses are refused.
alerts.telegramTokenHint: From @BotFather. Stored sealed and shown redacted after saving.
alerts.telegramChatIdHint: Numeric chat id; group and channel ids start with -100. Send the bot a message first, then read the id via getUpdates.
alerts.eventsHint: Leave empty to receive every event type.
alerts.channelDialogHint: Channels are shared by every alert source (security rules, certificates, agents).
alerts.historyHint: Every dispatched alert, newest first - security rules and control plane events alike. The history is written even when delivery fails.

sitePolicy.assignmentHint: A site follows one shared policy. Without one, the site keeps its own rules and settings.
sitePolicy.noneHint: This site uses its own rules and WAF settings. Pick a policy to share tuning across sites.
sitePolicy.assignFailed: Could not change the policy assignment
sitePolicy.overrideHint: Sparse deltas applied on top of the policy for this site only.
sitePolicy.overrideFormat: JSON keyed by layer kind, e.g. {"engine": {"mode": "monitor"}}. Only the keys you name override the policy.
sitePolicy.overrideShape: The override must be a JSON object keyed by layer kind
sitePolicy.overrideFailed: Could not save the site override
sitePolicy.effectiveHint: What the next configuration bundle will carry for this site.
sitePolicy.planHint: What the data plane will do with each managed rule for this site.
sitePolicy.applyHint: Published vs applied: a node that has not reported is unknown, never assumed applied.
sitePolicy.noRules: No policy rules reach this site.
sitePolicy.effectiveUnavailable: Effective configuration is unavailable right now.

dashboard.overview: Traffic, blocked requests and top talkers for the selected site and window. Drill into a site for its protection posture, or open Logs to answer why a request was blocked (each security event resolves its rule, policy and auto-block chain).
dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: Overview of your protected sites, agents and live threat activity.
dashboard.trafficOverviewDescription: Requests and blocked traffic over time.
dashboard.noTrafficDescription: Traffic data will appear here once your agents start proxying requests.
dashboard.topThreatIpsDescription: IPs generating the most blocked requests.
dashboard.noThreatsDescription: No blocked requests in the selected time window.
dashboard.noRulesTriggeredDescription: No WAF rules matched traffic in the selected time window.
dashboard.sitesTrafficDescription: Request volume over time for the busiest sites.
dashboard.noSiteTrafficDescription: Per-site traffic will appear here once your sites receive requests.
dashboard.topPathsDescription: Paths serving the most requests in the selected window.
dashboard.statusCodesDescription: Response status distribution in the selected window.

sites.overviewTitle: Every site is an edge configuration
sites.overview: Create a site, point its origin, then protect it: assign a shared policy or tune its own settings. Site status pauses serving without deleting configuration; the Web Protection tab shows what is actually in force, including published-vs-applied per node.
sites.title: Sites
sites.createDescription: Add a new site to protect with the WAF.
sites.emptyDescription: Add your first site to start protecting it with the web application firewall.
sites.noResultsDescription: No sites match "{{query}}". Try a different search.
sites.alternateDomainsHint: Optional. Every hostname here serves the same configuration as the primary domain. A wildcard such as *.example.com covers its subdomains but not the bare domain.
sites.domainDuplicate: "{{domain}}" is already served by this site
sites.deleteDescription: This action cannot be undone. All rules and logs for this site will be permanently removed.
sites.upstreamHint: Required. The edge forwards traffic here — the origin behind your CDN or WAF, e.g. origin.example.com:443.
sites.upstreamTlsHint: Connect to the origin over HTTPS.
sites.pauseDescription: The edge answers every request with a 503 maintenance page until the site is resumed. The TLS certificate, WAF logging and traffic counters keep running.
sites.resumeDescription: Traffic is routed to the origin again and every rule takes effect immediately.

failover.title: Disconnected behaviour (failover)
failover.description: What this site serves while the control plane is unreachable and the host has no synced rule bundle.
failover.defaultOpen: Global default: keep serving while disconnected.
failover.defaultClosed: Global default: refuse with 503 while disconnected.

origin.title: Origins
origin.description: Manage origin pools, load balancing and route dispatch.
origin.poolCreateDescription: An origin pool is a set of origin nodes sharing one load-balancing algorithm and origin protocol.
origin.poolEditDescription: Change the pool's load-balancing algorithm or origin protocol.
origin.poolsEmptyDescription: Create an origin pool to hold your origin nodes.
origin.nodesEmptyDescription: An empty pool cannot serve traffic — add an origin node.
origin.nodeDialogDescription: A node is an origin address that receives proxied traffic.
origin.nodeAddressHint: IP or hostname plus optional port, e.g. http://10.0.0.1:8080. A pasted scheme is dropped; paths are not allowed.
origin.nodeWeightHint: 1-10000; round robin splits traffic by weight
origin.lbHint: Round robin spreads by weight; hash pins similar requests to one node
origin.lbKeyHint: Header / cookie / query parameter name to hash on
origin.httpsOriginHint: Connect to the origin over TLS; requires the hostname on its certificate.
origin.sniHint: Hostname covered by the origin certificate; $host is not supported
origin.verifyCertHint: Turning this off skips certificate validation (not recommended).
origin.routesDescription: Dispatch requests to different pools by path; unmatched traffic goes to the default pool.
origin.routesEmptyDescription: All traffic currently goes to the default pool; add a route to split it by path.
origin.routeDialogDescription: Requests whose path matches the rule are forwarded to the target pool.
origin.priorityHint: 1-60000; empty uses the auto weight (exact 1024 / prefix 512 / regex 256)
origin.ipGroupHint: Only clients inside the group match this route; other clients fall through to the next route.
origin.deletePoolDescription: This cannot be undone; remove its nodes and route references first.
origin.deleteNodeDescription: The origin address will no longer receive traffic.
origin.deleteRouteDescription: Matching traffic will fall back to the default pool.

errors.nameRequired: Name is required, up to 100 characters
errors.lbKeyRequired: Hash algorithms need a key (max 64 characters total)
errors.sniRequired: An SNI hostname is required for HTTPS to origin
errors.sniTooLong: SNI hostname must be at most 255 characters
errors.sniInvalid: SNI must be a bare hostname without scheme or port, and not $host
errors.addressRequired: Origin address is required (host or host:port)
errors.addressPath: Enter host and port only — drop paths and query strings (the scheme is stripped for you)
errors.addressPort: Port must be an integer between 1 and 65535
errors.addressInvalid: Not a valid hostname or IP address
errors.weightInvalid: Weight must be an integer between 1 and 10000
errors.pathRequired: Path is required, up to 512 characters
errors.pathSpecial: Path must not start with = or ~
errors.pathRootPrefix: A prefix route on / conflicts with the default pool fallback
errors.priorityInvalid: Priority must be an integer between 1 and 60000

siteDetail.title: Site
siteDetail.pausedNote: This site is paused — the edge answers every request with a 503 maintenance page.

waf.overviewTitle: Rules that run on this site
waf.overview: Built-in managed rules and your custom rules, evaluated by the native engine. Severity, paranoia level and the site mode decide what reaches a verdict; rule tuning (disable, monitor, score, target exclusions) lives with the shared policy so one change applies everywhere it is assigned.
waf.title: Web Application Firewall

block.title: Block request
block.description: Deny the request immediately with the block response. Later rules are skipped.

challenge.title: Challenge the browser
challenge.description: Serve a browser challenge instead of the application; unresolved traffic is refused.

js_challenge.title: JavaScript challenge
js_challenge.description: Serve a proof-of-work JavaScript challenge first; passers continue to the application.

log.title: Record match, keep protecting
log.description: Record the match as a security event and keep evaluating; nothing is blocked.

allow.title: Exempt this request
allow.description: Stop evaluation for the request: later rules and managed blocks are skipped.

waf.advancedHint: Raw expression editor for complex rules
waf.customRulesHint: Rules you define to match specific traffic patterns.
waf.deleteRuleDescription: This rule will be permanently removed from the site.
waf.emptyDescription: The built-in rule pack is missing from this site. Restore it to protect against common attacks, then tune the rules as needed.
waf.enabledHint: Enable or disable this rule without deleting it.
waf.groupDialogDescription: Groups organise rules by phase and priority.
waf.groupHint: Assign this rule to a group (optional)
waf.groupsHint: Organise rules into groups with shared phase and priority.
waf.modeAlready: All rules already use this mode
waf.modeCardHint: Applies to all rules on this site.
waf.modeExplainer: Mode determines what happens when a rule matches: block drops the request, monitor logs it without blocking.
waf.noResultsDescription: No rules match the current filters.
waf.ruleDialogDescription: Define a WAF rule with conditions, action and metadata.

outcomes.offText: The rule is off - nothing is evaluated.
outcomes.monitorPrefix: Monitor mode: recorded as a monitor event;
outcomes.blockText: the request is denied with the block response and later rules are skipped.
outcomes.challengeText: the request must solve the challenge before it reaches the application.
outcomes.logText: the match is recorded as a security event; the request continues.
outcomes.allowText: evaluation stops for this request; later rules do not run.

waf.testHint: Evaluates the draft against this site's resolved configuration (policy rules, saved rules, patches) with the engine the edge runs. Rate limits, IP/geo and bot checks are edge decisions and are reported as skipped.
waf.ruleModeHint: Override the site-wide mode for this rule only.
waf.ruleNamePlaceholder: e.g. Block SQL injection in query
waf.tagsHint: Tags drive detection categories (e.g. sqli, xss, bot)
waf.restoreNothingHint: Every built-in rule already exists for this site.
waf.restoreDoneHint: They ship in monitor mode so you can see what they catch before blocking anything.

rateLimiting.overview: Rate limits run after bot checks and before the WAF engine: count requests per key (client IP, header, path) and answer bursts with block or challenge. Policy rules form the baseline; a site rule with the same path and method replaces it for this site only.
rateLimiting.title: Rate Limiting
rateLimiting.description: Protect against abuse and volumetric attacks by limiting request rates.
rateLimiting.emptyDescription: Create a rule to limit how many requests a client can make in a time window.
rateLimiting.characteristicsHint: How to group requests for counting (e.g. by IP, by path). Parameterized keys like header:X-Api-Key are also supported.
rateLimiting.characteristicFormatInvalid: Invalid characteristic — use header:<name>, cookie:<name> or query:<name>
rateLimiting.characteristicsRequired: At least one characteristic is required
rateLimiting.deleteDescription: This rate limit rule will be permanently removed.
rateLimiting.dialogDescription: Define request rate limits and mitigation actions.
rateLimiting.enabledHint: Enable or disable this rule without deleting it.
rateLimiting.expressionHint: Optional filter expression — empty means all requests
rateLimiting.mitigationHint: How long the action applies once triggered
rateLimiting.mitigationInvalid: Mitigation timeout must be between 0 and 86400 seconds
rateLimiting.periodInvalid: Period must be between 1 and 86400 seconds
rateLimiting.rulesHint: Rules are evaluated in priority order.
rateLimiting.thresholdHint: Maximum requests allowed in the period

bot.overview: Bot protection classifies user agents first: verified crawlers pass, browsers are checked against the enabled signals (JS challenge, TLS, behaviour), everything else receives the configured action. Verify claiming crawlers by DNS or by trusted IP range so a spoofed user agent cannot walk in on a name.
bot.title: Bot Protection
bot.description: Identify and mitigate automated traffic and malicious bots.
bot.jsDetectionHint: Run a JS challenge to verify real browsers.
bot.tlsFingerprintingHint: Match the TLS handshake against known libraries.
bot.actionHint: Applied to traffic classified as a bot.
bot.uaPatternHint: Substring matched against the User-Agent header.
bot.verifiedHint: A user agent claiming to be Googlebot & co. is cheap to forge. These checks trust the client only after it proves itself.
bot.verifiedIpHint: A client IP inside the referenced list passes regardless of its user agent.
bot.verifiedGroupHint: Import the crawler lists from the IP list catalog (e.g. All crawlers or a single service) to keep this group fresh daily.
bot.verifiedDnsHint: Known crawler user agents must reverse-resolve into the operator's own zones and that hostname must resolve back to the client IP; a spoofed claim receives the configured action.
bot.verifiedNote: DNS verification never blocks on outages: when the resolver fails, the check degrades to the user-agent verdict instead of guessing. Verdicts are cached per IP and crawler family.

cc.overview: CC protection challenges clients that exceed the burst thresholds instead of blocking them outright. Under Attack Mode challenges every visitor - turn it on during an attack and off afterwards; clearance never bypasses the IP, rate-limit or WAF layers that follow.
cc.title: CC Protection
cc.description: Detect and challenge HTTP flood (CC) attacks in real time.
cc.enableHint: Challenge clients that exceed the rate threshold.
cc.minutes: Minutes a solved challenge stays valid.
cc.rateThresholdHint: Requests per minute per IP before a challenge.
cc.checksHint: Additional signals used to classify clients.
cc.tlsFingerprintHint: Compare the TLS handshake fingerprint against known clients.
cc.exemptPathsHint: Paths that bypass CC protection (press Enter to add).

protection.settingsOverview: The engine choice, enforcement mode and paranoia level decide how the rules run on this site; monitor-only downgrades keep detection active while recording instead of blocking. When a policy is assigned, its layers override these settings - local deltas belong in the site overlay on the Policy tab.
protection.title: Web Protection
protection.description: WAF posture, rule grading and CC protection for this site.
protection.policyBanner: This site follows policy {{name}} (rev {{n}}). The policy overrides the settings on this page; local deltas belong in the site overlay.
protection.advancedModeHint: Enables the strict managed rule set and deep request-body inspection.
protection.engineHint: Which engine inspects this site. Inherit follows the deployment default; Shadow compares both engines without changing enforcement; Varman enforces the new pipeline escalated with the legacy verdict; Legacy-only disables the new pipeline for this site.
protection.customLayersHint: Per-site rules evaluated at the edge. Both layers can only add protection - they never weaken the native engine.
protection.virtualPatchesHint: SecLang rules (the OWASP CRS dialect) evaluated by the native engine. Rules with a block/deny action block matching requests; the source is validated before it is saved.
protection.openapiSpecHint: Requests are checked against the declared operations: an undeclared path under the spec's base prefix, an undeclared method or a missing required query parameter is recorded as a monitor event.
protection.performanceHint: Higher interception rate at a proportional performance cost.
protection.monitorHint: Turn a family or stack off to keep detecting and logging its matches without blocking them.
protection.categoryLinkageHint: Switching a category to monitor-only also downgrades its managed rules of the same family - literal-expression rules only follow the per-rule list. Switching it back resets those family overrides; the switch is disabled until the rule catalogue loads, so the two lists always move together.
protection.monitorExplainer: A switched-on downgrade keeps detection fully active but records instead of blocking. Language-agnostic detections are never downgraded by a stack switch.
protection.underAttackHint: Challenges every visitor with a JavaScript check. Turn it on while your site is under an active attack.
protection.underAttackActiveHint: All visitors are challenged. Turn it off once the attack subsides.
protection.underAttackConfirmDescription: Every visitor will be challenged and CC protection will be switched on. Keep it on only as long as the attack lasts.

protectionOverview.noPolicy: No shared policy - this site runs on its own settings
protectionOverview.followsHint: The policy's layers are compiled into this site's bundle; local deltas belong in the site overlay on the Policy tab.
protectionOverview.noPolicyHint: Assign a policy on the Policy tab to share posture and rules across sites; unassigned sites keep their own settings.
protectionOverview.pathHint: Left to right is the runtime order. A terminating answer (block, challenge, deny) returns immediately and skips every later stage.

stages.ipDetail: IP rules and geo decisions run first; {{n}} shared rule(s) resolved from the policy.
stages.botDetail: Verified crawler allowlists, browser checks and challenges gate the request next.
stages.rateDetail: {{n}} shared limit(s) plus the site's own path limits.
stages.rulesDetail: {{rules}} custom rule(s), {{plan}} compiled managed/CRS rule(s), plus patches and API schema when set.
stages.challengeDetail: Challenge gates for bursts and the site-wide Under Attack switch.

protectionOverview.orderNote: Short-circuits are explicit: an IP/geo denial or a bot denial answers before rate limits, and rate limits answer before the WAF engine. The engine's mode (off / monitor / block) caps every rule path.
protectionOverview.modulesHint: Choose a module to review its status or edit its configuration for this site.

modules.botHint: Crawler allowlists, browser proof and private-device confirmation.
modules.rulesHint: Site rules and policy rules evaluated by the engine.
modules.crsHint: Paranoia levels, disabled rules, score overrides and imported CRS rulesets - all in the policy model.
modules.accessHint: Allow, block or challenge addresses and countries before the WAF runs.
modules.rateHint: Count requests per key and path, then block or challenge bursts.
modules.ccHint: Burst detection and the site-wide challenge gate.
modules.settingsHint: Engine choice, advanced mode, paranoia level and monitor-only downgrades.

ipRules.title: IP Access Rules
ipRules.description: Allow, block or challenge traffic from specific IP addresses and ranges.
ipRules.dialogDescription: Rules are evaluated before the WAF.
ipRules.emptyDescription: Add a rule to allow or block specific addresses.
ipRules.ipHint: A single address or a CIDR range such as 10.0.0.0/24.
ipRules.name: Rule name
ipRules.groupHint: The rule always uses the group's latest ranges.
ipRules.rangesHint: One IP or CIDR per line.
ipRules.manualNone: Enter at least one valid IP or CIDR.
ipRules.summaryHint: IP rules take precedence over WAF rules. {{grouped}} reference IP groups.
ipRules.bulkHint: One IP or CIDR per line.
ipRules.invalidGeneric: Enter a valid IP address or CIDR range.

invalid.empty: Enter an IP address or CIDR range.
invalid.prefix: Prefix length is out of range.

autoBlocked.title: Auto-blocked IPs
autoBlocked.description: IPs the edge currently refuses for this site after WAF or rate-limit verdicts. The list refreshes from agent heartbeats.
autoBlocked.unblockDescription: The edge stops refusing this IP immediately on every enforcing node.
autoBlocked.emptyDescription: IPs blocked by WAF or CC defenses will appear here with their attack history.

caching.title: Caching
caching.description: Configure edge caching rules and purge cached content.
caching.dialogDescription: Define what the edge stores and for how long.
caching.rulesHint: Rules are evaluated in order; the first match wins.
caching.emptyDescription: Create a rule to start caching content at the edge.
caching.matchExpressionHint: Leave empty to match every request.
caching.cacheEligibleHint: Allow matching responses to be stored.
caching.purgeHint: Evict specific URLs or the entire site cache.
caching.purgeEmpty: Enter at least one URL to purge.
caching.purgeAllDescription: This evicts every cached object for the site. This cannot be undone.
caching.activationHint: Off by default. Turning it on restores the built-in rules and enables every cache-eligible rule at once.
caching.activationSwitchHint: Rules keep their own switches; this one flips all of them together.
caching.activatedNotice: The built-in rule set is now live: static assets, HTML pages and the /api/ exclusion are active on every edge.
caching.enableDescription: {{enabled}} rules are live; {{inserted}} of {{total}} built-in rules restored.
caching.disableDescription: {{count}} rules were turned off; the rules themselves are kept.
caching.noEligibleRulesHint: This site has no cache-eligible rule. Restore the built-in rules, or mark a rule as cache eligible.
caching.restoredDescription: {{inserted}} of {{total}} built-in rules inserted; they start disabled.
caching.cacheHeaderNote: is returned on every response with hit / miss / stale / revalidated, so a single curl is enough to check cache behaviour.
caching.usageHint: Reported by the edges; refreshes every 30 seconds.
caching.noEdgeReport: No edge has reported cache usage for this site yet — the counters stay empty until an agent sends its first heartbeat. The configured quota is already in effect.
caching.noQuotaNote: The quota is 0 (unlimited), so no ceiling is enforced on the edges.
caching.quotaHint: One budget for the whole site, shared by every cache rule.
caching.quotaFieldHint: Shared by every cache rule of the site; 0 means unlimited.
caching.quotaInvalid: Enter a whole number of MiB between 0 and 1048576.
caching.quotaNotPerRule: Disk quota is a site-wide setting — see the Site disk quota card above the rule table.
caching.purgeResult: {{delivered}} edges notified now · {{queued}} queued for the next heartbeat

ssl.title: SSL/TLS
ssl.description: Manage certificates, ACME automation and TLS settings.
ssl.addCertDescription: Issue automatically with ACME or upload your own certificate.
ssl.emptyDescription: Add a certificate to serve HTTPS for this site.
ssl.acmeEmailHint: Used for expiry notices by the CA.
ssl.pemRequired: Both certificate and key are required.
ssl.hstsHint: The edge adds Strict-Transport-Security to HTTPS responses so browsers keep using HTTPS.
ssl.hstsMaxAgeHint: Seconds browsers remember the policy. The edge sends no header while this is 0; 15552000 (180 days) is a common choice.

accessControl.title: Access control
accessControl.description: Allow or deny traffic by IP address and geography, and gate requests behind HTTP basic credentials.

lifecycle.title: Request lifecycle
lifecycle.description: Where every VarmanWAF feature acts in the proxy pipeline. Use this map to see which stage your WAF, IP, bot, rate-limit and cache rules run in, and to debug why a request was allowed, blocked or challenged.

tls.title: TLS & connection
tls.desc: The TLS handshake happens before any HTTP processing: SNI selects the certificate, and when any site enables mTLS the listener verifies client certificates against the union of trusted CAs (per-site enforcement runs in the WAF plugin).

earlyRequest.title: Early request
earlyRequest.desc: The location (host + path) is matched and the request context is created, then every early_request plugin runs: the WAF plugin's full check chain (below) and the challenge verify endpoint /_varman/challenge/verify. A plugin answering here short-circuits every later stage.

request.title: Request
request.desc: ACME HTTP-01 and metrics requests are answered here (after passing the WAF above), then the location path rewrite and request-step plugins run: the rewrite plugin and the cache plugin (per-session cache setup, PURGE handling). A request matching no location gets a 404 without running any plugin.

cacheLookup.title: Cache lookup
cacheLookup.desc: Pingora's built-in HTTP cache. A hit ends the request without contacting the upstream — but the request already passed the WAF and rewrite. A miss continues to the upstream.

upstream.title: Upstream
upstream.desc: The load balancer picks a backend (with retries on connect failure), X-Forwarded-* style headers are appended, and the body is streamed upstream; oversized bodies are rejected with 413.

upstreamResponse.title: Upstream response
upstreamResponse.desc: The upstream response headers arrive: pingora decides whether the response may be stored in the cache, and the error page plugin can replace upstream error responses (400+, including 502/504) with the site's custom pages.

response.title: Response
response.desc: Response-step plugins run: the WAF plugin records status and size for the access log, the per-site HSTS plugin adds Strict-Transport-Security, and cache headers (Age, …) are added. Response body filters then rewrite the body — except after a 101 upgrade, where the bytes are WebSocket traffic.

responseBody.title: Response body
responseBody.desc: At end of stream the WAF plugin emits the access log entry (with the response body sampled per the site's logging settings).

failure.title: Failure
failure.desc: Only on errors: classified as 502 upstream error / 499 client gone / 408 read timeout / 400 invalid header, then rendered with pingap's built-in error template. No plugin runs here, so custom error pages cannot replace this page.

logging.title: Logging
logging.desc: pingap writes its own access log last. VarmanWAF's entries were already emitted at the stage where the decision was made: generated responses (blocks, challenges, pause pages) at request time, regular responses when the body completes.

lifecycle.wafDescription: The checks run in this order on every request; the first one that answers ends the request.

paused.title: Paused site
paused.desc: A paused site answers with the pause page immediately — nothing else runs.

mtls.title: mTLS client certificate
mtls.desc: A missing or invalid client certificate is blocked at the site level.

access.title: IP & geo rules
access.desc: First match wins (priority ascending). Actions: block, allow, challenge, js_challenge — or basic_auth, deferred to the next check.

basicAuth.title: Basic Auth
basicAuth.desc: Site-wide or triggered by an IP/geo rule. Failed attempts get a small delay; unauthenticated requests get the 401 page. hide_credentials strips the Authorization header.

bot.title: Bot protection
bot.desc: User-agent classification: pass, deny (block page) or log only.

rateLimit.title: Rate limiting
rateLimit.desc: Fixed-window counters per rule (IP, host, path, header, cookie…). Over the threshold the rule's action runs; challenge can issue a clearance cookie.

engine.title: WAF engine
engine.desc: Signature and expression rules with an anomaly score. Verdicts: pass, monitor (log only), block, challenge.

lifecycle.tipsDescription: Common questions answered by the lifecycle order.

observation.title: Observation mode
observation.desc: Detections keep running but block/challenge verdicts are only recorded as "would have blocked". Paused sites, mTLS and Basic Auth are still enforced.

firstMatch.title: Order matters
firstMatch.desc: IP and geo rules evaluate top-down and the first match wins — an allow rule above a catch-all block decides the outcome.

cache.title: Cache never bypasses the WAF
cache.desc: Checks run before the cache lookup, so cached hits are inspected like any other request, and a block always wins over a cached response.

customPages.title: Custom error pages
customPages.desc: Error pages replace upstream error responses. WAF block/challenge pages are generated before the upstream is contacted and keep their built-in design.

responseCache.title: Response edits and the cache
responseCache.desc: The cache stores the response as it leaves the upstream phase. Response-phase changes — rewrite response rules, HSTS — run after the cache on every serve (cache hits included), so the stored copy stays unmodified; error-page replacements are sent with no-store and never stored.

blockedIps.title: IP Blacklist
blockedIps.description: Every dynamic block in force across your sites — WAF/rate-limit auto-blocks and manual blocks — with one-click unblock and manual blocking. Refreshes with agent heartbeats.
blockedIps.overview: Every dynamic block in force across the fleet: WAF and rate-limit auto-blocks plus manual blocks, each row folded per site and IP with its attack history. Manual blocks fan out to every registered agent and are queued for offline ones; the list reconciles from agent heartbeats, so a block disappears once every node reports it lifted.

blockedIps.emptyDescription: IPs blocked by WAF or rate limiting show up here with their attack history, and you can block IPs manually.

configHistory.title: Configuration history
configHistory.description: Every recorded configuration version across the deployment and its sites, with the snapshot each one captured.
configHistory.overviewTitle: Roll back with evidence, not guesswork
configHistory.overview: Each change to site or deployment-wide settings records a version: what it touched, who made it and when. The detail view shows the snapshot's per-table counts; a rollback restores that scope exactly, is recorded as a new version itself and pushes the restored configuration to the agents immediately. The CLI (`varman config history`) reads the same record.
configHistory.adminOnly: Configuration history and rollbacks are administrator-only; ask an administrator if you need a restore.
configHistory.detailEmpty: This version recorded no table rows.
configHistory.detailNote: The stored snapshot is the restorable document; rolling back replaces the scope's tables with exactly these rows.
configHistory.rollbackDescription: Restores the {{scope}} scope exactly as version #{{id}} recorded it. Every table in that scope is replaced, the rollback is recorded as a new version, and the restored configuration is pushed to the agents immediately. This cannot be undone except by another rollback.
configHistory.rolledBack: Restored {{scope}} to version #{{restored}}; recorded as version #{{created}} and pushed to the agents.
configHistory.emptyDescription: Configuration versions appear here as soon as a change is recorded for this scope.

reports.overviewTitle: Summary here, full report on demand
reports.overview: The console loads only the aggregates below. The complete report - interception types, daily timeline, attack-IP and URL rankings - is built when you generate it and downloads as a self-contained HTML file: no scripts, no external assets, opens offline and prints to A4. Generation is bounded (92 days maximum, top-20 lists), so the control plane stays light.
reports.adminOnly: Reports are administrator-only; ask an administrator for a copy.
reports.generateHint: The report covers the selected range and scope; it is generated on demand and downloads immediately.
reports.settingsHint: What the generated report prints on its cover; saved for every future generation, including scheduled ones.
reports.heading: Heading
reports.headingHint: Shown on the cover page and in the browser tab.
reports.footerNoteHint: Printed above the data-source note on the last page.
reports.settingsSaveFailed: Could not save the report settings
reports.windowDaysHint: The report covers this many days, ending at the trigger time.
reports.scheduleHint: Saved with the heading; enabling arms the schedule so the first report goes out at the next occurrence. Reports dispatch through the alerting channels - e-mail channels attach the HTML file, chat channels receive the summary - and every run is recorded in the alert history.
reports.summaryHint: Interceptions recorded in the selected range.
